text: Kailas Nath Wanchoo (25 February 1903 – 14 August 1988) served as the tenth Chief Justice of India. He was born in Allahabad into a Kashmiri Pandit family and received his primary education in Nowgong, Madhya Pradesh, and middle education at Pandit Pirthi Nath High School, Kanpur, Muir Central College, Allahabad, and Wadham College, Oxford. He joined the Indian Civil Service as Joint Magistrate on 1 December 1926 in Uttar Pradesh. Wanchoo was appointed as a Judge of the Allahabad High Court on 17 February 1947. In April 1967, he was sworn in as Chief Justice of India after Koka Subba Rao retired from the position to announce his presidential campaign. During his tenure on the Supreme Court, he authored 355 judgments and presided over 1,286 benches. As Chief Justice of India, he administered the oath of office to the third President of India, Zakir Husain. This Indian law–related biographical article is a stub.
